- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture downside risk.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.3–0.8% bias to early periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to reflect reversion bias.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.75–0.85), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1.5% below recent peak to avoid overbought bias.
